full_judgment:
2. Pre-emptor respondent filed Miscellaneous Case No. 26 of 1988 in the 6th Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka for pre-emption of the case land as a co-sharer and contiguous owner of the same. The case was contested by the petitioner. Trial Court by judgment dated 30.8.1990 allowed pre-emption. Being aggrieved by the same petitioner preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 190 of 1990 and court of appeal below by judgment and order dated 29.3.1995 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and order of the trial court and dismissed the pre-emption case. Being aggrieved by the same petitioner moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2138 of 1995. A Single Judge of the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 18.8.1997 made the rule absolute. Being aggrieved by the same petitioner has filed this petition for leave to appeal. 

 3. Learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that as WAPDA canal is running through the suit land WAPDA is a necessary party and such necessary party having not been impleaded the court of appeal below rightly held that the case was bad of defect of parties. He further submits that the canal having divided the case land one part of pre-emptor's land is contiguous to the case land and the other part is not and as such pre-emptor can get only the contiguous part and not the other part and this will give rise to partial pre-emption which cannot be allowed under law. 

 4. After going through the impugned judgment we find that the petitioner did not raise the question of the defect of party at the trial and the land in which WAPDA constructed the canal has not yet been finally acquired. We further find that in spite of the canal running through the case plot the same has not been legally divided. In view of the above we find no illegality in the impugned judgment and no merit in the submissions.
